items.title: Welcome by the School Board President, Cecilia Márquez
Additions, Deletions, or Modifications to the Agenda

publicComments.name: Chris R.
publicComments.summary: Raised legal concerns about using Prop 39 bond money for workforce housing under Article 13 of the California Constitution, questioned whether teachers actually want district housing, and suggested alternative funding mechanisms such as a parcel tax or housing vouchers.

publicComments.name: Elizabeth Starks
publicComments.summary: A multilingual Redwood City resident and former ESL teacher who expressed support for retaining good teachers but emphasized the greater need for after-school spaces and resources for children left unsupervised in the community.

publicComments.name: Maria Stockton
publicComments.summary: As leader of the classified union chapter, she defended the equal importance of classified staff, shared her own experience of rent increases outpacing raises, and expressed strong support for workforce housing to help staff who commute long distances remain in the community.

publicComments.name: Lupe Guzmán
publicComments.summary: The principal of Hoover Community School expressed strong support for workforce housing, noting that staff who live in the community strengthen it and that housing stress causes new teachers to leave the district.

publicComments.name: Mary
publicComments.summary: A visiting San Francisco school board member asked about the quality and durability of the construction and how the rental revenues flow relative to the bond repayment.

publicComments.name: Janet Cochise
publicComments.summary: A parent in the district since 2008 described how school closures and teacher departures due to unaffordable housing have repeatedly disrupted her child's education, and raised concerns about inadequate student transportation.

publicComments.name: Erin Washburn
publicComments.summary: President of the Redwood City Teachers Association confirmed that teachers do want workforce housing, sharing examples of colleagues whose lives improved with affordable housing and expressing support for the plan as a way to recruit and retain quality teachers.
